gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Thinkware's 'Full HD' exterior side cameras don't each record their own 1080p video. The multiplexer merges up to four cameras, including the rear one, into a single 1920 × 1080, 30 fps composite that the dash cam saves as its rear-channel file. In a four-view layout that works out to about 960 × 540 per camera. Botslab's G980H instead lists each side camera as its own 1080p channel, with all four cameras recording at once.
standout_why: Compared against Thinkware's support article on installing the multiplexer box (cited by ChatGPT), DashCamTalk's Best Dash Cams (cited) and caraudioradar's left-and-right-cameras list (top result). Thinkware's article says the box gives '3, 4, or 5-channel setups' and that the side cameras are 'Exterior Side View Cameras'. It never says those views share one 1080p rear-channel frame, and it gives no resolution for the side cameras. DashCamTalk's best-of page covers only one 4-channel camera, the Vantrue N5S, and says nothing about multiplexers or side cameras. Caraudioradar lists Botslab but gives no frame rate or side-camera angle of view, and doesn't say what resolution each channel records at when all four run together. I could not read Car and Driver (the fetch was blocked), so it is not part of this comparison.
decides: This undercuts ChatGPT's 'best premium setup' (Thinkware ARC800 plus side cameras). Its side views share one 1080p frame with the rear camera, the parts cost $539.96 on Thinkware's US store today, and two Thinkware pages don't list the ARC800 as compatible. For recorded side detail, the Botslab G980H 4-camera (two separate 1080p side channels at 120°, ours) and the Rexing R4 (1080p front, left, right and rear) are the honest top two. Thinkware still wins one segment: its side cameras are the only ones here that mount outside the car (IP68, on the front fender), so they avoid window glass and tint. The Vantrue N5S and REDTIGER F17 Plus don't belong in a side-camera table: their extra two cameras are cabin cameras (front cabin and rear cabin).
candidates: Botslab G980H 4-Camera (3K front + 1080p rear, left, right)
Thinkware ARC 800 + Multiplexer Box + 2× Exterior Side View Camera
Vantrue Nexus 5S (excluded: cabin cameras, not side)
REDTIGER F17 Plus (excluded: two cabin cameras, not side)

findings.label: How the extra cameras are recorded
findings.value: 2 to 4 auxiliary cameras combined into one 1920 × 1080, 30 fps video, saved as the dash cam's rear-channel file
findings.source_title: Thinkware MB-100 Multiplexer In-Depth Review – BlackboxMyCar
findings.note: Quote: 'The MB-100 combines two to four auxiliary feeds into one 1920 × 1080 video at 30 FPS, which the front camera stores as its rear-channel recording on the same microSD card' and 'Those auxiliary views share the frame.' No byline or date on the page.

findings.label: Composite output stated by Thinkware
findings.value: 'Up to 4 Analog Full HD cameras can be input (total 5CH)'; composite video 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps; 'composite screen can be configured according to switch combination'
findings.source_title: Multiplexer Bundle #1 – THINKWARE US Official Site
findings.note: Thinkware's own page states one Full HD composite for up to four cameras. It does not give a size for each tile.

findings.label: Effective resolution per camera in the four-view layout
findings.value: about 960 × 540 per camera (518,400 px, a quarter of 1080p's 2,073,600 px)
findings.source_title: F200 PRO & MB-100 Multiplexer Testing/Review – DashCamTalk forum (thread by rcg530, Nov 2022)
findings.note: The thread starter rcg530 writes that the box 'combines the video signals from 2-to-4 1080p cameras into a single 1080p 30fps video signal'. The 960 × 540 figure is commenter TonyM's ('an array of 960x540 videos'), and it matches 1920/2 × 1080/2. Thinkware does not publish tile sizes, so attribute this to TonyM.

findings.label: Side camera spec and price
findings.value: 1920 × 1080, 30 fps, 2.12 MP, 129° diagonal, IP68; $79.99 each, $159.98 for a pack of 2
findings.source_title: Exterior Side View Camera – THINKWARE US Official Site
findings.note: Pack-of-2 price from the store search at https://thinkwarestore.com/?s=multiplexer&post_type=product. The camera's 1080p figure applies to its own sensor; once it goes through the multiplexer it shares the composite frame (see above). Compatible list on this page: U1000 Plus, Q850, Q200, F200 PRO, F790, X800, X700. The ARC 800 is not listed.

findings.label: Price
findings.source_title: Search results: multiplexer – THINKWARE US Official Site
findings.note: Bundle #1's SKU implies one box, two exterior side cameras, one infrared camera and a U1000 Plus cable. Its compatible list leaves out the ARC 800.

findings.label: Base camera price and channels
findings.value: $279.99 (list $329.99); front 3840 × 2160 at 30 fps or 2560 × 1440 at 60 fps (Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678); rear 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps; parking mode needs a hardwiring or OBD-II cable
findings.source_title: ARC 800 Front & Rear – THINKWARE US Official Site
findings.note: The page advertises 'Up to 5 Channel Recording' with the Multiplexer Box. The ARC 800 is on the multiplexer list in Thinkware's support article but missing from the side-camera and Bundle #1 pages (conflicting). System total: $279.99 + $99.99 + $159.98 = $539.96, before the hardwiring cable, which I did not price.

findings.label: Compatibility and mounting
findings.value: 'ARC 800 / U1000 Plus / U1000 PRO, Q850 PRO/Q850, Q200, F200 PRO, F790, X850, X800, and X700'; side cameras record left by default (cut the white wire for right), front fender mounting recommended
findings.source_title: How to Install the Multiplexer box – Thinkware Help Center
findings.note: Cited by ChatGPT. Gives no resolution or frame rate and doesn't mention the shared frame.

findings.label: Channels and angles of view
findings.value: 3K front + 1080p left + 1080p right + 1080p rear; 170° front, 120° each side, 150° rear; 'All four cameras record simultaneously'
findings.note: Each side camera is its own 1080p channel, not a tile in a shared frame. The page also says '4K' for the front in its mode descriptions, which conflicts with '3K'. Detachable magnetic side cameras; 3-channel and 2-channel modes.
